subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the centroid and the area of the triangle formed by the lines 2y² − xy − 6x² = 0 and x + y + 4 = 0.

mark_split.label: Split the pair into two lines

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 4 PAIR OF STRAIGHT LINES, Short Answer question 14(ii), book p.169. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split is 1+1+1+1 for the same reason as its companion question 14(i): the pair has to be factorised, the two vertices found, and only then can the centroid and the area each be written — four equal actions, four equal marks. The area was cross-checked against the standard formula n²√(h² − ab) / |am² − 2hlm + bl²|. Written as ax² + 2hxy + by² this pair has a = −6, 2h = −1 so h = −1/2, and b = 2; with l = 1, m = 1, n = 4 the formula gives 16(7/2)/|−6 + 1 + 2| = 56/3, matching the coordinate calculation. Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. LINES EXPANDED 2026-09-14 (founder direction, modelled on the Maths-2A, Maths-2B and Maths-1A expansions): every move is written on its own line, with the reason or the arithmetic shown before it is used; the steps, marks and split are unchanged.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say where the third vertex is, and how you keep the fractions straight in the centroid.

steps.label: Split the pair into two lines
steps.margin_note: First mark. The pair is written with y² first, so read the terms carefully before splitting: 2 × (−6) = −12 and (+3)(−4) = −12 with 3 − 4 = −1. Always multiply the factors back out.
steps.memory_tip: Written y² first, so read the coefficients before splitting: 2 × (−6) = −12 and 3 − 4 = −1.

recall.must_convey: That the pair factorises as (y − 2x)(2y + 3x) = 0, checked by multiplying the factors back out.

steps.why: A homogeneous second-degree equation with h² ≥ ab is two lines through the origin, whichever variable is written first. Once it is factorised the question is an ordinary coordinate-geometry question about three known lines.
common_mistakes: Reading the xy coefficient as h instead of 2h, so h = −1 instead of −1/2.
Taking a = 2 and b = −6 because y² is written first, when a is the x² coefficient.

steps.label: Find the two vertices
steps.margin_note: One mark. Both lines of the pair pass through the origin, so O is the third vertex, with no work needed. Here vertex A carries fractions, so keep them as fractions and do not round.
steps.memory_tip: Both lines of the pair pass through the ORIGIN, so O is the third vertex, with no work needed.
lines: Both lines of (1) pass through O(0, 0).

recall.must_convey: That the three vertices are O(0, 0), A(−4/3, −8/3) and B(8, −12).

solve each line of the pair with the given line

steps.why: Solving each factor separately with the given line keeps each solve a plain pair of linear equations, which is where the fractions stay easiest to control.
common_mistakes: Rounding −4/3 to −1.3 and losing the exact area later.
Solving the given line against itself instead of against a factor.
lines_compact: Both lines of (1) pass through O(0, 0).

steps.label: Find the centroid
steps.margin_note: One mark. Add the three x values as fractions first, then divide by 3. The divisor 3 sits outside, so a third of a third gives ninths in the answer.
steps.memory_tip: Add the three values as fractions FIRST, then divide by 3 — that is where the ninths come from.

recall.must_convey: That averaging the three vertices gives the centroid (20/9, −44/9).

steps.why: The centroid needs all three vertices, unlike the area, which can be written from two of them when the third is the origin.
common_mistakes: Averaging only the two vertices found by solving.
Writing thirds in the answer instead of ninths.

steps.label: Find the area
steps.margin_note: The last mark. With one vertex at the origin the area determinant becomes ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁|. Cross-check with n²√(h² − ab)/|am² − 2hlm + bl²|, where h = −1/2 and h² − ab = 49/4: that also gives 56/3.
steps.memory_tip: With a vertex at the origin the determinant becomes ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁| — only two points appear.

lines.text: (the area formula with one vertex at the origin)

lines: With O a vertex, Δ = ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁|

recall.must_convey: That the area is ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁| = ½(112/3) = 56/3 sq.units.

steps.why: The second product x₂y₁ = 8(−8/3) is negative, so subtracting it adds. That is why the two numbers combine to 16 + 64/3 and do not cancel.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign in y₁ = −8/3, which turns 16 + 64/3 into 16 − 64/3.
Leaving the answer as 112/3 by forgetting the factor ½.
lines_compact: With O a vertex, Δ = ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁|
